claims.text: Role in hypokalemia: high single oral doses cause GI irritation, so deficits are usually replaced in divided doses;
claims.quote: Because high single doses can cause GI irritation and occasional bleeding, deficits are usually replaced in divided doses.

claims.text: a 1 mEq/L ↓K ≈ a 200 to 400 mEq total deficit, replaced over several days at 20 to 80 mEq/day.
claims.quote: Because a decrease in serum potassium of 1 mEq/L (1 mmol/L) correlates with approximately a 200- to 400-mEq (200 to 400 mmol) deficit in total body potassium stores, total deficit can be estimated and replaced over a number of days at 20 to 80 mEq (20 to 80 mmol)/day.

claims.text: IV KCl: arrhythmia: central vein, max 40 mEq/h, only w continuous cardiac monitoring; routine IV ≤ 10 mEq/h;
claims.quote: For hypokalemic arrhythmia, give IV potassium chloride through a central vein at a maximum of 40 mEq (40 mmol)/hour and only with continuous cardiac monitoring; routine IV infusion should be no more than 10 mEq (10 mmol)/hour.

claims.text: avoid dextrose diluents (insulin can transiently worsen hypokalemia).
claims.quote: Dextrose or glucose solutions used for dilution are avoided because elevation in the serum insulin concentrations could result in transient worsening of hypokalemia.

claims.text: Potassium chloride ER (KCl) dose, hypokalemia: Tx of K depletion: 40 to 100 mEq/day or more.
claims.quote: Doses of 40 to 100 mEq per day or more are used for the treatment of potassium depletion.
The dose for the prevention of hypokalemia is typically in the range of 20 mEq per day.

claims.text: Divide dosage if more than 20 mEq/day is given so no more than 20 mEq in a single dose.
claims.quote: Dosage should be divided if more than 20 mEq per day is given such that no more than 20 mEq is given in a single dose.

claims.text: Take w/ meals and a glass of water; ⍉ on an empty stomach (potential for gastric irritation).
claims.quote: Potassium chloride extended release tablets should be taken with meals and with a glass of water or other liquid. This product should not be taken on an empty stomach because of its potential for gastric irritation

claims.text: Potassium chloride ER (KCl) safety: CI: hyperkalemia (further ↑ serum K can produce cardiac arrest).
claims.quote: Potassium supplements are contraindicated in patients with hyperkalemia since a further increase in serum potassium concentration in such patients can produce cardiac arrest.

claims.text: CI: any structural, pathological, or pharmacologic cause for arrest or delay in tablet passage through the GI tract.
claims.quote: All solid oral dosage forms of potassium chloride are contraindicated in any patient in whom there is structural, pathological (e.g., diabetic gastroparesis), or pharmacologic (use of anticholinergic agents or other agents with anticholinergic properties at sufficient doses to exert anticholinergic effects) cause for arrest or delay in tablet passage through the gastrointestinal tract.

claims.text: In pts w/ impaired K excretion, potassium salts can produce hyperkalemia and cardiac arrest; potentially fatal hyperkalemia can develop rapidly and be asymptomatic.
claims.quote: In patients with impaired mechanisms for excreting potassium, the administration of potassium salts can produce hyperkalemia and cardiac arrest. This occurs most commonly in patients given potassium by the intravenous route but may also occur in patients given potassium orally. Potentially fatal hyperkalemia can develop rapidly and be asymptomatic.

claims.text: ⍉ treat hypokalemia w/ concomitant potassium salts and a potassium-sparing diuretic (e.g., spironolactone, triamterene, or amiloride): severe hyperkalemia.
claims.quote: Hypokalemia should not be treated by the concomitant administration of potassium salts and a potassium-sparing diuretic (e.g., spironolactone, triamterene, or amiloride) since the simultaneous administration of these agents can produce severe hyperkalemia.

claims.text: Closely monitor K w/ concomitant RAAS therapy (ACE inhibitors, ARBs, spironolactone, eplerenone, or aliskiren).
claims.quote: Drugs that inhibit the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) including angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), spironolactone, eplerenone, or aliskiren produce potassium retention by inhibiting aldosterone production. Closely monitor potassium in patients receiving concomitant RAAS therapy.

claims.text: Closely monitor K w/ concomitant NSAID therapy.
claims.quote: Closely monitor potassium in patients receiving concomitant NSAID therapy

claims.text: Discontinue immediately and consider ulceration, obstruction, or perforation if severe vomiting, abdominal pain, distention, or GI bleeding occurs.
claims.quote: Potassium chloride extended release tablets should be discontinued immediately and the possibility of ulceration, obstruction, or perforation should be considered if severe vomiting, abdominal pain, distention, or gastrointestinal bleeding occurs.

claims.text: Careful monitoring of serum K and appropriate dosage adjustment required in chronic renal disease or any condition impairing K excretion.
claims.quote: The use of potassium salts in patients with chronic renal disease, or any other condition which impairs potassium excretion, requires particularly careful monitoring of the serum potassium concentration and appropriate dosage adjustment.

claims.text: OD: hyperkalemia is usually asymptomatic and may be manifested only by an ↑ serum K (6.5 to 8 mEq/L) and ECG changes (peaking T-waves, loss of P-waves, S-T depression, QT prolongation).
claims.quote: hyperkalemia is usually asymptomatic and may be manifested only by an increased serum potassium concentration (6.5 to 8 mEq/L) and characteristic electrocardiographic changes (peaking of T-waves, loss of P-waves, depression of S-T segment, and prolongation of the QT-interval)

claims.text: OD tx: IV calcium gluconate if the pt is at no risk or low risk of developing digitalis toxicity.
claims.quote: Intravenous calcium gluconate if the patient is at no risk or low risk of developing digitalis toxicity.
